newsitem.title: CANADA: TransCanada Pipe to change issue terms.
newsitem.headline: TransCanada Pipe to change issue terms.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said on Thursday it agreed with the province of Alberta to change the redemption terms of the C$150 million 10.426 per cent convertible subordinated debentures held by the province.
When they were issued to the province in December 1991, the debentures were convertible at the holder's option into TransCanada common shares at a price of C$23.041.
They were also redeemable by TransCanada between June 20, 1995, and December 20, 1996, only in certain circumstances depending on the market price of TransCanada's common shares.

Under the new terms, the debentures may be redeemed in whole or in part at par by TransCanada at any time up to December 20, 1996, by the issue of that number of TransCanada common shares such that when the province resells them, results in net proceeds to the province equal to the principal amount of the redeemed debentures, the company said.

Should TransCanada elect to redeem some or all of the debentures on or prior to December 20, the province will immediately resell the shares in Canada. Additional amounts owing on the debentures, primarily accrued interest, will be paid in cash on the redemption date.
Failing an earlier election, the debentures will continue to be redeemable in accordance with their original terms after December 20, 1996.
